title: Polyphase surge controller and tenant utilization telemetry
author: Marcus Chen
release_notes: Introduce a polyphase surge controller to smooth tenant bursts and new utilization telemetry rollups for more accurate per-tenant headroom accounting; no API contract changes.
description: Summary: Adds a 'polyphase' surge controller that staggers temporary burst allowances across short, medium, and long time windows to avoid synchronized warm-pool pressure during cross-tenant spikes. Also introduces a lightweight tenant utilization rollup pipeline (percentile + EWMA sketches) consumed by the autoscaler and the Console. Motivation: recent incidents showed many tenants taking simultaneous short bursts which forced large warm-pool spin-ups and produced noisy utilization signals. The polyphase approach spreads transient credits and produces smoother admission decisions while preserving short burst responsiveness. Key changes: 1) controller/core/polyphase_controller.go: new algorithm and decision interface; 2) controller/api/telemetry_ingest.go: new rollup ingestion path and schema; 3) telemetry/rollups/percentile_sketch.go: compact sketch implementation tuned for low-cardinality tenant series; 4) autoscaler/integrations.go: uses rollup ETS metrics to adjust warm-pool sizing; 5) console/frontend/tenant-utilization.tsx: new per-tenant 50/90/99 histograms and a 'burst posture' indicator; 6) e2e/bench/scale_surge_test.go: regression test and load harness. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1324) - [x] Unit tests for sketch and controller - [x] Integration test with warm-pool emulator - [x] Console visualization wired to telemetry - [x] Backwards-compatible telemetry schema (ingest uses feature-flag) Behavior notes: - Polyphase credit windows: 1s (immediate), 30s (short), 5m (sustained). Credits are proportional to tenant commitments with soft upper bounds; controller may defer granting long-window credits if warm pool headroom is low. - Rollups publish: p50, p90, p99, ewma rate, and a burstiness score (0-1). - Default behavior behind feature-flag rollout for 2 weeks then enabled cluster-wide. Commits: ["feat: add polyphase controller core and interfaces", "perf: compact percentile sketch with streaming merge", "chore: telemetry schema version bump and feature flag", "feat: console burst posture UI and API wiring"]. Files changed (high level): ["controller/core/polyphase_controller.go", "controller/core/polyphase_controller_test.go", "telemetry/rollups/percentile_sketch.go", "telemetry/rollups/percentile_sketch_test.go", "telemetry/ingest/ingest_pipeline.go", "autoscaler/integrations.go", "console/frontend/tenant-utilization.tsx", "console/api/handlers/telemetry.go", "e2e/bench/scale_surge_test.go", "deploy/k8s/configmap-rollup.yaml", "scripts/bench/run_surge_harness.sh", "docs/ops/polyphase-deploy.md"]. Runtime impact: microbenchmarking shows 6-8% CPU overhead on the telemetry pipeline at peak ingest but reduces warm-pool spin-ups by ~22% in simulated multi-tenant surge tests. Reviewed perf tradeoffs and added sampling thresholds to avoid unbounded cost. Backwards compatibility: ingest preserves v1 schema; rollup feature requires opt-in flag. Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary clusters (2 days) -> regional pools (5 days) -> global (toggle off if regression).
